learning_goal: Teach learners to understand and apply the main ideas of 'Energy — How Things Work'.

explanation_sections.title: Connect
explanation_sections.explanation: Begin with learners' prior experience related to Energy — How Things Work and invite predictions.

explanation_sections.title: Explore
explanation_sections.explanation: Use the chapter evidence below to build the explanation rather than introducing unsupported facts.
source_evidence: In Grades 3 and 4, students have engaged with local toys like (spinners and paper boats) to understand how they work.
They have also learned about how things are made by exploring the processes of bricks, paper, etc.

While making things with locally available materials students learn useful methods of sustainable development, including refuse, reduce, reuse, repurpose and recycle (the 5 R s) so that they can make responsible decisions.
By making things with their own hands, they develop a deeper appreciation for the materials we use in everyday life, and also learn to connect and care for their environment.

explanation_sections.title: Make meaning
explanation_sections.explanation: Ask learners to explain what the evidence shows, compare ideas, and justify answers.

explanation_sections.title: Apply
explanation_sections.explanation: Move from a chapter example to a new, closely related example.

teaching_sequence.teacher_action: Model close reading/working with the chapter.

teaching_sequence.student_action: Explain why an answer is supported.

misconceptions: Giving an answer without explaining the reasoning.
checks_for_understanding: What evidence in 'Energy — How Things Work' supports your answer?
Can you explain the idea in your own words?
closure: Ask the learner to state the most important idea and one way it can be used.
